note: Built only from headlines and outlet summaries of the last 48 hours. Probabilities are estimates, not certainties, and nothing here is financial advice.
big_picture: Trump is now signalling an end to the Iran war: after meeting Qatar's prime minister he spoke of "positive momentum", called the war "effectively over" militarily and said more strikes "don't seem necessary", while staying "locked and loaded". Qatar has delivered a ceasefire proposal. Oil kept falling (Brent about $92, −10% in a month) and chip stocks bounced hard, but Nvidia itself fell on new reports that it intervened in a US chip-smuggling probe. In Washington, a Republican (Massie) is forcing a House vote this week to impeach Defense Secretary Hegseth over the war, and some Republicans say it could pass. The Russia–Ukraine–US talks in Abu Dhabi start on 10–11 November, and the Trump–Xi(–Putin) meeting in China is next week. The Houthis are not part of Trump's de-escalation and keep hitting Saudi targets.

stories.title: US–Iran war: Trump talks of an end, Qatar brings a ceasefire proposal
stories.reality: The US is winding the war down after the midterm losses showed how unpopular it is: Trump calls it militarily "effectively over" and sees "positive momentum" after a 45-minute meeting with Qatar's prime minister, who delivered a ceasefire proposal. No deal exists yet, the naval blockade stays, and Trump keeps the threat of strikes. The conflict goes on at the edges: the US moved aircraft out of a second UK base over an Iranian threat, and France blamed Iran's Revolutionary Guards for a cyberattack on about 700 supermarkets' fridges and wants EU sanctions.
agreed: Trump and Qatar's prime minister both called their talks "positive"; Trump spoke of "positive momentum toward an end to this conflict".
Qatar delivered a ceasefire proposal (Al Jazeera, Middle East Eye).
Trump says further military action "doesn't seem to be a very necessary thing" but the US is "locked and loaded" if anything changes.
Rubio and Hegseth defend the war as "necessary", while admitting it is not popular.
France says IRGC hackers took over refrigeration controllers at around 700 retail sites last month; it summoned Iran's ambassador and will seek EU sanctions.

against: Netanyahu, reportedly calling Trump every day to push for resuming the war (Times of Israel)
The US moving aircraft out of UK bases over an Iranian threat (WSJ via Times of Israel, TWZ)
disputed.note: Talk of an end is coming from Washington and Doha; nothing has been heard yet from Tehran on the ceasefire proposal.

disputed.claim: The Gulf states want the Hormuz blockade kept
against: Trump to Reuters: Qatar and Saudi Arabia "would rather see a peaceful solution" (Middle East Eye, TASS)
disputed.note: Both can be true: a ceasefire first, with the blockade as leverage for a later deal.

stories.title: Houthis keep hitting Saudi Arabia: Aramco tower, East-West pipeline
stories.reality: The Houthis are not part of Trump's de-escalation. After damaging the Aramco tower in Riyadh, they hit the East-West pipeline (Saudi Arabia reported damage) and fired more missiles at Riyadh, which were intercepted. No official word on lost oil flow. The pipeline matters because it lets Saudi oil bypass Hormuz to the Red Sea.
agreed: Saudi authorities reported damage to the key East-West pipeline (Al Jazeera).
Saudi forces intercepted two missiles fired at Riyadh hours later.
The Aramco tower in Riyadh's financial district was hit by "falling shrapnel", with no one hurt (NYT).

disputed.claim: The attacks have cut Saudi oil flows
against: No confirmation from Saudi Arabia or Aramco
disputed.note: The same pipeline was out for weeks after a drone attack in September; a repeat would matter for oil.

framing.how: Lead with the Saudi line: little damage, missiles intercepted.

stories.title: Ukraine: US–Russia–Ukraine talks open in Abu Dhabi
stories.reality: The first three-way talks since February are on 10–11 November, with Medinsky leading Russia's delegation. The US says it wants a "final end" to the war and a "long-term security architecture" between Moscow and Europe. A ceasefire is not on the table, and the old sticking point is unchanged: Ukraine wants security guarantees that Russia rejects. Europe pushes for a seat; the US proposes bringing Europeans in after the three-way round. Drones killed two workers at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear and thermal plants.
agreed: The Russian and Ukrainian delegations have left for Abu Dhabi; talks are set for 10–11 November (TASS, Anadolu).
Security guarantees are the top item, per Rubio and Lavrov; prisoner exchanges are also on the agenda.
Trump sees a "strong inclination" to end the war.
India spoke with both sides ahead of the talks.
The IAEA condemned drone strikes that killed two power plant workers at Zaporizhzhia.

for: France / NPR: European officials will attend
against: Reuters via TASS: the US proposes bringing Europeans in only after the three-way talks
The IAEA and Kyiv Independent don't assign blame

framing.how: Procedural, and Ukraine blamed for the plant attack.
The US's ambitious "final end" goal and Trump's optimism.
Low expectations: no ceasefire on the table, the same sticking points.

predictions.statement: The Abu Dhabi talks take place with Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations

stories.title: Nvidia: the Huang affair widens to a chip-smuggling probe
stories.reality: The story has moved from the CEO's private life to the company's conduct. NYT and Bloomberg report that a Commerce Department inquiry into Megaspeed, a Singapore buyer of Nvidia chips suspected of supplying China, was halted after a top Nvidia executive contacted officials, and passed to the Justice Department. Trump says the FBI is reviewing the affair but backs Huang. Nvidia fell again (−4%) even as other chip stocks bounced strongly, so the market now prices company-specific risk. Google's new AI chips add competition.
agreed: Trump says the FBI is reviewing Huang's relationship and that Xi may raise the case; he believes Huang didn't know.
The Commerce inquiry into Megaspeed went to the Justice Department after an Nvidia executive contacted Commerce officials (NYT, Bloomberg).
Lawmakers from both parties want to question Huang.
Nvidia fell while the chip sector rallied; Asian tech stocks had their best two days in three months as oil fell.

disputed.claim: Nvidia improperly interfered with the Megaspeed probe
against: No public response from Nvidia in the collected articles

framing.how: Corporate conduct: the halted Megaspeed probe.
Key-person risk and a valuation test; Megaspeed's China links.

stories.title: Washington: House vote to impeach Hegseth over the Iran war
stories.reality: Republican Thomas Massie filed eight articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Hegseth and is forcing a House vote, possibly on Wednesday. Democrats back it, and several Republicans privately say it could pass. Republicans still hold the outgoing House, so leadership can try to table it. Even if the House impeaches, conviction in the Senate needs two-thirds, which is very unlikely. Elsewhere: the Senate advanced a bipartisan permitting bill 73–25 (pipelines, power lines, data centres pay for their own grid upgrades), and Jeffries says Democrats will target tariffs, Medicaid cuts and the Iran war in January.
agreed: Massie introduced eight articles of impeachment and forced a privileged vote this week.
Democrats, led by Jeffries, back it; Trump and Rubio defend Hegseth.
The Senate voted 73–25 to advance the permitting bill.
Democrats' priorities for January include ending Trump's tariffs.

disputed.claim: The impeachment will pass the House
for: A member of Congress to The Intercept ("high chance")
against: Republican leadership can move to table it; Trump is pressing Republicans (Al Jazeera)

framing.how: Hegseth deserves impeachment for an "unconstitutional war".
A test of Congress over the Iran war.

stories.title: China: a $1 trillion trade surplus before the Trump–Xi(–Putin) meeting
stories.reality: China's trade surplus passed $1 trillion in ten months, a record pace: exports rose 35.2% in October and imports grew at the fastest pace in five years. That raises trade tension just as Trump goes to China next week. Trump says he will meet Xi and Putin there and wants their help to end the Iran war; WSJ reports the US balked at China's demand for a tightly scripted three-way summit.
agreed: Exports +35.2% year on year in October (expected +33.5%); the surplus is above $1 trillion for the first ten months.
Trump expects to meet Xi and Putin during his China visit next week.

framing.how: The surplus will intensify tensions with trading partners.

stories.reality: Eisenkot has up to six weeks and is reaching out to Netanyahu's allies; analysts see several routes but formidable obstacles. In Washington, bipartisan support for Israel is eroding: Democrats push to limit military aid, and Vice President Vance is among Republicans calling for change.
agreed: Eisenkot was tasked with forming a government and has up to six weeks.
He warns Israel is near a "point of no return".

market_calls.why: Oil fell 8% in a month on peace-talk hopes, but a US–Iran deal looks unlikely (15%), more US strikes are likely (60%) and the Houthis keep hitting Saudi targets. The risk premium is more likely to come back than to fade.
War risk in the Gulf, falling US yields (10-year down 8% in a month) and a possible US shutdown all support gold.

Three-way Ukraine talks with Europe at the table this week (85%) keep "peace" headlines coming. A real ceasefire is unlikely (12%), so the drop should be modest, and much is already priced in (Rheinmetall is −57% from its high).
Airlines rallied hard (+20% in a month) as oil fell. If oil's risk premium returns, they are the first to give it back.

Down 26% in a month: a lot of bad news is priced in. The Trump–Xi meeting (85% it happens) can bring a relief rally on export rules. This is a short-term bounce call, not a call that the selloff is over.
About 120x earnings, falling even after beating expectations, and AI-bubble worries hit the whole sector. Momentum is down (−19% in a month), but strong growth limits the downside.

Trump is winding the Iran war down, Qatar has a ceasefire proposal on the table, and Congress is turning against the war (the Hegseth impeachment vote). ITA rose 3.9% on the last day, so part of the risk premium can fade. Barely better than a coin flip: defence budgets don't change with one ceasefire.
